title: Choose the visual world for RIFTBALL
question: The roll assigned The Tapestry Hall. Keep it, take the alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Tapestry Hall
options.lineage: Angers Apocalypse and Bayeux narrative tapestries, hung from iron rods in a timber great hall
options.thesis: The world is woven: every week becomes a scene stitched into the hall's tapestries.
options.viewport: Heraldic banners hang from an iron rod as the navigation; the week's stories are one woven frieze, scenes alternating madder red and woad blue, Latin-style captions above each; a 26-row woven season band shows woven, current and bare warp weeks.
options.risk: Woven texture done timidly reads as a brown theme; it must be saturated red and blue fields, not beige.

raised.raise: Weld-gold thread is reserved for 'now and next' only: the current week, the Weave action, the followed path.
Each screen holds one monumental woven centrepiece; everything around it stays quiet.
The 26-week season loom is one ruling axis that every screen positions itself against.
Matches carry an explicit threshold vocabulary: sealed, unfolding, revealed, with the wax seal as the irreversible step.
Stitch-on motion: threads draw themselves in as state changes, already drawn under reduced motion.
In the arena, selecting an athlete isolates their thread through the match and dims everyone else.

options.label: The Illuminated Codex
options.thesis: The game is one great open book; every screen is a folio, ribbons are the navigation.
options.viewport: A two-page spread on a dark desk: the week's lead story with a historiated initial on the left, tidings on the right, ribbon bookmarks as the sections.
options.risk: The most familiar destination for medieval UI, and a cream-parchment ground that every model reaches for first.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.thesis: Every screen a decision point with one yellow band telling you where next.
options.viewport: Yellow bands listing clubs and fixtures as gates.
options.risk: Breaks the pinned medieval world entirely.
options.case: Clear navigation, but players do not see a fantasy sport in an airport.
options.kept: One reserved signal colour used only for where you are and what comes next.

options.label: Fashion Flagship
options.thesis: Athletes as looks, one at a time, in vast white space.
options.viewport: One athlete portrait full-screen with a giant serif name.
options.risk: Sparse where the game needs dense statistics.
options.case: Elegant but loses both the medieval world and the data depth.
options.kept: One monumental centrepiece per screen, quiet around it.

options.label: Accretion Threshold
options.thesis: The Rift as a gravitational well pulling clubs toward the crown.
options.viewport: A glowing disk with clubs orbiting the Grand Rift.
options.case: Striking but contradicts the pinned fantasy world.
options.kept: Explicit threshold states for results: sealed, unfolding, revealed.

options.label: Deep Dive
options.thesis: Descend through the season like depth stages.
options.viewport: A vertical season axis descending through weeks.
options.kept: One ruling axis, the season, that every screen positions against.

options.label: Hand-drawn Zine
options.thesis: The rules of Riftball sketched like a friend's napkin.
options.viewport: Doodled pitch diagram with mascot callouts.
options.risk: Too casual for a premium fantasy game.
options.case: Funny, matching the voice, but not a premium video game.
options.kept: Draw-on motion tied to state changes.

options.label: Event Display
options.thesis: Each match as a frozen collision of tracks.
options.viewport: Match events as tracks curling out of kickoff.
options.case: Clever for replays only; loses the world everywhere else.
options.kept: Select one athlete to isolate their thread through the match, dimming the rest.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Classic fantasy RPG chrome: dark carved panels with gold trim, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar of framed buttons, framed panels in a grid, gold headings.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every fantasy game menu; close to a dark dashboard.
